body:
Owner intent: make the LSP integration world class and use Corvint capabilities to provide the best possible information across use cases. This extends, and does not reopen or overstate, completed Go milestone V1-0476. Owner decision: BOTH upstream language-server enrichment for agents and a Corvint editor language server. The direction is accepted; technical profiles and qualification thresholds remain proposed. Current evidence: Go/gopls-specific provider, definition/reference expansion, fixed bounds, external evidence separated from ranking; no broad multi-language or outcome qualification. Existing V1-0168 workspace-loading and V1-0167 error-redaction tickets remain separate work and must be dispositioned with evidence. Do not treat every Corvint command as mandatory runtime work or claim support for every possible use case; define tested profiles and explicit unsupported cases.

# Bidirectional LSP quality plan — V1-0477

Owner decision: BOTH upstream language-server enrichment for agents and a Corvint language server for editors. This direction is accepted by the owner's chat response; technical profiles, language order, performance thresholds and promotion remain proposed. Existing Go integration V1-0476 is delivered and stays experimental. This plan is not a delivery claim.

## Product boundaries

Use one shared evidence compilation interface behind CLI/MCP and an optional native-Go stdio editor companion. The editor starts and owns the companion session; shutdown, EOF, cancellation and interruption retire its descendants. Core remains usable as one terminating native-Go binary with no required daemon, network service, account or new database. The companion and each upstream provider require a separately explicit deployment/execution profile. Do not turn on every Corvint tool for every request.

Maintain two distinct snapshot identities: immutable Git evidence (repository/root, object format, commit/tree/blob) and live editor overlays (session, canonical document URI, monotonically validated document version and content digest). Never label overlay text as committed evidence. Corvint context for committed content remains usable separately when a live view cannot be represented. Results identify their snapshot; stale/out-of-order responses cannot replace newer results. Close/save/reopen, branch changes, renames, root changes, generated files and Unicode positions need fixtures. Git status alone is not an editor buffer identity.

Compile applicable facts through existing trust boundaries: project-owned specs/instructions retain authority; upstream semantic facts, history and inferred relationships remain labelled evidence. Expose relevant definitions/references/types, impact, governing requirements, tests and actual test observations, CEM/OCM/frontier gaps, source documentation and explicit uncertainty. Learning/ranking changes require their own accepted contracts and frozen evaluation; never silently turn separated LSP evidence into a ranking input. Test suggestions, formatting/refactoring/rename edits and code actions are proposals, not permission to execute commands or modify files.

## Stages and dependencies

1. Contract and baseline: freeze the numbered capability/session/profile spec and requirements-to-tests matrix. Inventory languages, server versions, editors and workspace types; distinguish consumed, delegated, Corvint-enriched and unsupported capabilities. Register public representative fixtures plus a held-out corpus without reading protected existing holdouts. Define numerical quality/resource/latency targets from a recorded baseline before implementation or promotion; include baseline language-server-only and Corvint-only arms.
2. Upstream adapters (after 1; reuse V1-0168 and V1-0167): capability negotiation, executable/config identity, workspace loading, URI/encoding boundaries, cancellation, errors, no silent installs/downloads, and hostile response bounds. Repair loading and redact diagnostics before treating provider availability as success. Expand beyond Go only through independently qualified language/server/workspace tuples. Proposed first cross-language candidates are TypeScript and Python; order is not yet accepted. Adapter metadata maps each method to advertised support, limits and degradation reason, not a blanket language-supported boolean.
3. Shared snapshots and evidence joins (after 1): implement and test the immutable/overlay model, shared semantic query interface, provenance, stable identities, duplicate/conflict handling, budgets, invalidation and trust-preserving joins. Reuse existing Core/index contracts rather than adding a second authority store. Cross-language/framework links require witnessed evidence; absence is unknown. All consumers see the same underlying facts for the same admitted snapshot and request, though transport projections can differ.
4. Editor LSP companion (after 2 and 3): initialization/capability negotiation, document sync, request cancellation, diagnostics lifecycle, shutdown/exit/EOF, multi-root isolation and position encodings. Expose negotiated standard features through qualified upstream delegation and Corvint enrichment; expose Corvint-only evidence via documented namespaced extensions or editor commands. Capability matrix includes navigation, hover/signatures, completion, symbols, diagnostics, call/type hierarchy, semantic tokens/inlay hints, rename/refactoring/formatting and code actions; advertise only actually implemented/tested subsets, and keep edits version-checked and client-applied. Verify real VS Code and a second independent LSP client; existing VS Code integration is deferred under its own contract and is not reopened implicitly.
5. Agent integration (after 2 and 3): bounded task-specific semantic requests in CLI and MCP through the shared engine, explain selected providers/features and omissions, avoid unnecessary fan-out, preserve committed default output and cancellation/cleanup. A richer/longer-lived opt-in profile is explicit; ordinary CLI reads do not require the editor server. No automatic model calls, test execution or learning. Compare joined semantic evidence to prior packets with authority and uncertainty invariant tests.
6. Qualification and promotion (after 4 and 5): deterministic conformance plus real repos/workspaces, cross-language boundaries, missing dependencies, dirty buffers, rapid edits, branch/root changes, malicious/oversized output, provider crashes and cleanup. Freeze correctness/coverage floors, stale-result rejection, cold/warm p50/p95, memory/CPU, query/token cost and task outcomes per declared profile. Compare upstream-only, Corvint-only and combined arms. No world-class/superiority claim from synthetic parity, implementation presence or native evidence linkage alone. Publish supported/degraded/unsupported tuples with measured limits, rollback and explicit failed/unrun evidence. Keep parent open until delivered, integrated and qualified.

Current code: internal/lspprovider/provider.go, internal/lspevidence/context.go, docs/LSP.md.
